text:
Toronto's four-game winning streak ended in Calgary, and the Flames pushed their own run to four straight by scoring twice in the final 90 seconds. Joel Farabee made it 4-2 at 18:35 of the third, Martin Pospisil added an empty-net-era dagger at 19:21, and a game that had been one goal apart for 12 minutes finished 5-2. Matvei Gridin led the way with two goals and an assist. The 2024 first-round pick (28th overall) scored 79 points in 56 QMJHL games for Shawinigan last season, and his first-period goal came on a 3% chance, the least likely goal of the night.

The way the game was played was closer than the score. Our numbers give Calgary a 56% chance of deserving the win, based on simulated replays of every shot, and the Flames had the better expected goals (the quality of chances) at 4.44 to 2.86. Much of that gap came late: Calgary's third-period expected goals were 2.15 against Toronto's 0.90. At even strength the two sides were level, 2.18 to 2.14. Auston Matthews had the best look Toronto got, a 51% chance in the first period that Devin Cooley stopped. Matthews still reached 800 career points with an assist on William Nylander's goal that cut it to 3-2. Cooley saved 0.86 goals more than expected, while Sergei Bobrovsky was roughly average at 0.25.

Calgary now has four straight wins and looks sturdy through three periods. Toronto drops its first game after a four-game run, and the two late goals made the loss look bigger than the play was.
